content.text: Places the instructions were unclear or left to test empirically: (1) The grammar never states whether `/pattern/` for read/write ranges matches as substring or whole-line — discovered empirically that `/status:/` matches by substring, causing an ambiguity refusal on two lines. (2) `--exclude GLOB` semantics (root-relative-path vs basename matching, and whether it crosses `/` into subdirectories) were never exercised — task 1 was resolved by grepping the whole tree unfiltered and manually excluding `vendor/` and `build/` hits, since --grep with no excludes already surfaced every match. (3) The "-M form not supported in write plans" claim held, but the resulting error ("bad line number \"\"", exit 2) is a plan-parse failure, not the per-hunk "refusal names the file, the plan line, and the reason" format the instructions describe for refusals elsewhere — a wording gap, not a bug. (4) Nothing was left dangling: only reads and two intentional writes to `docs/meta.yaml` (net change: `status: final` → `status: done`) ran; the failed `/status:/` and `-2` attempts wrote nothing, as promised.

Places the instructions were unclear or left to test empirically: (1) The grammar never states whether /pattern/ matches as substring or whole-line — found empirically that /status:/ matches by substring, causing an ambiguity refusal on two lines in meta.yaml. (2) --exclude GLOB semantics (path-vs-basename matching, whether it crosses "/" into subdirectories) were never exercised — task 1 was resolved by grepping the whole tree unfiltered (which already surfaced vendor/ and build/ hits) and excluding those two files manually, rather than relying on --exclude. (3) The -2 (from-the-start) form is confirmed unsupported in write plans, but the resulting error ("bad line number \"\"", exit 2) is a plan-parse failure, not the per-hunk "refusal names the file, the plan line, and the reason" format described elsewhere for refusals — a documentation/wording gap, not a functional bug. Nothing left dangling: only reads plus two intentional writes to docs/meta.yaml ran (net effect: line 3 "status: final" -> "status: done"); the two negative-test writes (task 8's ambiguous /status:/ attempt, task 9's -2 delete attempt) both failed as designed and wrote nothing.
